rationale: C06 contains a distinctive celebratory-letter formulation addressing a national or state leader and transmitting goodwill “to you and through you to the people,” closely mirrored by the child’s wish to “convey through you to the people of Alaska” the new flag. That specific intermediary-address construction, combined with the shared ceremonial tone and concluding good wishes, plausibly supplied a reusable drafting template. C20 and C25 are weaker parallels involving governors, admission to the Union, the people of the new State, and best wishes, but lack the child’s distinctive phrasing.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I should like to express my great pleasure at being able to convey through you to the people of Alaska the first flag of new design in forty seven years.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I send my greetings and best wishes, as well as those of the people of the United States, to you and through you to the people of Pakistan.
shared_material.explanation: Both use the addressee as the intermediary through whom a ceremonial message or object is conveyed to the people represented.

shared_material.parent_excerpt: May I express my good wishes for success in these worthy endeavors.
shared_material.explanation: The letters share a formal celebratory close reinforcing the parallel intermediary-message structure.
